question: How did the acquisition of zamindari rights of Sutanuti, Gobindpur, and Kalikata in 1698 affect the legal status of the English East India Company in India?
options: It made the EIC a sovereign independent state in Bengal.
It integrated the EIC into the Mughal administrative structure as a local landholder (zamindar) subject to Mughal revenue laws.
It exempted the EIC from paying any land revenue to the Mughal state.
It allowed them to expel all Mughal administrative officers from Bengal.
explanation: Purchasing the zamindari of the three villages legally made the EIC a vassal of the Mughal Empire in terms of land tenure. They had the right to collect land revenue and administer justice locally, but they paid a fixed annual land revenue (jama) to the Mughal treasury.

question: By 1700, the English East India Company had organized its administration into three main presidency seats in India. Which of the following correctly identifies these three presidencies?
explanation: By 1700, the EIC's administration was organized into three main presidencies: Bombay (which replaced Surat as the western seat in 1687), Madras (Fort St. George, established 1639-40), and Calcutta (Fort William, established 1700).
